checks.bounds: base: 2 VAT buckets, 2 payment/PTD slots, 1 Final Invoice slot, one issueFinalInvoice and one PTD correction in flight, both regimes (24,800 distinct states); wide: 3 slots
assumptions: Every service method is one CoreStore transaction; the memory store serializes transactions and Postgres row-locks with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE at READ COMMITTED in S4 order (Proforma first)

Only issueFinalInvoice and correct/cancel of a PTD are split at their row-lock acquisitions; every other method is one step because what it decides on cannot change under it: it holds the lock every writer of that row takes (Payments.remove reads the PTD unlocked, every PTD writer locks the Proforma first) or the value only moves one way (loadForCredit's unlocked Final Invoice read can only become reversed)
A failed transaction writes nothing and releases its locks
Amounts are abstract units per VAT bucket; VAT, rounding and CZK math belong to verify-vat-numbering-math
Document Lock is modelled on the Proforma and the Final Invoice only; on a PTD it only disables correct/cancel
The Issuing Entity's regime is fixed for a run (both regimes are explored)
Regimes vat_payer and non_vat_payer only; identified_person is out of scope

checks.bounds: 30 traces on TestCore (vat_payer and non_vat_payer): the shortest path to each model action, guard traces, both serial orders of H2, the D7 cap for PTDs and the Final Invoice, four crash points (CNB fixing unavailable during PTD and Final Invoice issue; Credit Note and Final Invoice numbering exhausted); model invariants checked after every step
assumptions: In-memory store: transactions run serially, so the H2 overlap itself is not replayed (pg-contention job)
Crash points only where a seam exists: FixtureRates.unavailable and a numbering series at its last counter (Workspaces.configureSeries)

checks.bounds: base: 1 occurrence, 2 recurring workers, 2 crashes at any crash point, 1 duplicate or stale start, 2 provider failures (5 outcomes incl. outcome_unknown sent/not sent), 2 dispatch attempts per execution; wide (nightly): 2 occurrences, 1 provider failure, 2 attempts; mutants: 1 occurrence (2 for skip-occurrence), 1 crash
assumptions: Each transaction is one step: the schedule row lock (issuance.ts lockSchedule) and the memory store's serialized transactions make it atomic; Postgres locking is not checked here (pg-contention)
DocumentDelivery runs keyed by the delivery id: a start for a live execution attaches to it (J1); modelled as one execution slot per delivery
The base enables the designed J1a OutboxReconcile for queued/sending deliveries (core-ports J1a); core at 77a5bb7 has none, so H3 is CONFIRMED on the code (mutants no-reconcile-*, replay FINDING H3)
J3 eligibility re-check, pauses, catch-up cap and detach are left out: the document stays sendable and the schedule active
The provider may accept a message twice (no dedupe assumed); fairness per component: sweep, reconcile, each job execution

checks.bounds: one schedule, TODAY's occurrence, one delivery per run; replays: the happy path, duplicate/concurrent and repeated starts, a same-day second tick, crashes after issue commit, inside the send transaction, before the start hook, after claim (H3: stranded on core's own recovery; recovered by the designed J1a), after the provider accepted, and before giveUp; provider not_accepted / rejected / outcome_unknown
assumptions: In-memory CoreStore (serialized transactions); Postgres row locks are the pg-contention job's
Crash points use existing seams: a RecurringRepo or DeliveryJobs or EmailSender wrapper that dies, and not running the next step
Recovery tests other than FINDING H3 play the designed J1a delivery reconcile by calling deliver; core has no cross-tenant query for queued/sending deliveries
The sealed System caller is taken from a RecurringSweep tick (no export of the seal)

checks.bounds: base: 2 issues from stored drafts, 1 override, 2 periods, MaxSeq 3, 1 pre-issued document, a rollback at any statement that is not waiting, deadlock checked; 29,127 distinct states, exhaustive within the bound. wide: adds 1 issue from input; 324,673 distinct states. A second override is outside every bound (over 28.6 million states)
assumptions: One Workspace, one DocumentKind, one YYYY-NNNN series: reservation keys include workspace and kind, and distinct sequences format to distinct numbers (Numbering.format, covered by verify-vat-numbering-math)

Steps are Postgres READ COMMITTED statements on the committed schema: counters.lock is SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on numbering_counters; reservations.tryReserve is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on number_reservations_pkey, which waits for an open inserter of the same key, and a free key for a document without a row fails number_reservations_document_fk (no Postgres CoreStore exists yet; the in-memory store serializes whole transactions and has no foreign keys)
A waiting transaction does not crash (no lock timeout), so a wait cycle is reported as a deadlock
Manual override numbers range over the series' own number space; numbers outside it cannot meet the allocator
Not modeled: configure(nextNumber) raising the counter (an intended gap, W3), pattern changes, Credit Note, Payment Tax Document and correction numbering

checks.bounds: 11 hand-written serial traces (9 projections of Numbering.tla traces within the TLC bounds, 1 override of an override beyond them, 1 issue from input that commits only in memory) plus 100 seeded sampled traces of 6 steps checked against the model's serial transitions (property test, not exhaustive, not within a TLC bound)
assumptions: In-memory store: one top-level transaction at a time and no foreign keys, so only serial projections of model traces replay, with the foreign-key check passing; statement interleaving and the number_reservations_document_fk failure under Postgres are left to the pg-contention job
Documents are read back through Documents.get after each step; reservations are probed with tryReserve in a transaction that always rolls back

checks.bounds: 5 requests (r1, r2 edit from revision 1 on one key with different payloads; r3 edits from revision 1 on its own key; r4 creates; r5 edits from revision 2 on r3's key), overlapping attempts per request 2,1,2,2,1 (8), any attempt may abort before COMMIT; wide: 2 attempts of every request (10)
assumptions: One Contact row edited by Contacts.save stands for every Collection.getForUpdate/update and checkRevision caller; one create stands for every insert behind withIdempotency

CoreStore port semantics as documented in CoreStore.ts: a claim on a key pending in another transaction waits until that transaction ends; rollback drops the pending claim and row locks (memory.ts runFrame; a SQL adapter must match)
Body writes, requestLog.complete and the audit row are transaction-local until COMMIT, so they form one step; Abort models any failure, defect or interruption before COMMIT
Request-key TTL (24 h) never expires inside a run: replay after expiry re-runs the body by design and is not modelled; scopes other than one Workspace are not modelled
MCP preview -> confirm tokens are not modelled: core has no confirmation-token issuance or redemption yet (only api-contract helpers in packages/api-contract/src/mcp.ts)
Contacts.save's same-content no-op edit (returns the row unchanged, no revision bump) and IČO unique-index conflicts (ensureIcoFree, UniqueViolation) are not modelled

Executes getForUpdate/update, not checkRevision (Expenses is its only caller)
